# jamovi: inference for two odds or two proportions  {#jamoviChisquare}



```{block2, type="rmdobjectives"}
**Topics** covered in this chapter:
  
* How to use jamovi for comparing two odds (i.e., analysis using odds ratios).
* How to use jamovi for comparing two proportions.

```


## Introduction {#B12Data}

RQs comparing *two qualitative variables* require count data that can be compiled into a two-way table of counts. 
Consider data [@data:Gammon2012:B12] [in Exercise\ 31.16 of the textbook](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/AnalysisOddsRatio.html) (Table\ \@ref(tab:jamoviB12Data)).



```{block2, type="rmddatafile"}
The data file (`B12-Long.csv`) can be downloaded in Sect. \@ref(DataFiles).
You can download the data, and follow the instructions.
```


**This data set is available from the textbook as `B12-Long`** in 
[Appendix\ A](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/AppendixDataSets.html).
You can download the data and follow along if you wish.

There are *two qualitative variables* being measured on each individual:

1.  Whether the person is vegetarian (or not);
1.  Whether the person is B12 deficient (or not).

Hence, jamovi will have *two columns*: one for each variable.
There are $124$ units of analysis, so there are *$124$ rows* of data.


```{r jamoviB12Data,  echo=FALSE}
B12Data <- array( dim = c(3, 3) )

rownames(B12Data) <- c("Vegetarians",
                       "Non-vegetarians",
                       "Total")
colnames(B12Data) <- c("B12 deficient",
                       "Not B12 deficient",
                       "Total")

B12Data[1, ] <- c(8, 26, 34)
B12Data[2, ] <- c(8, 82, 90)
B12Data[3, ] <- c(16, 108, 124)

if( knitr::is_latex_output() ) {
  kable(B12Data,
        format = "latex",
        booktabs = TRUE,
        longtable = FALSE,
        align = c("r", "r", "r"),
        caption = "The number of vegetarian and non-vegetarian women who are (and are not) B12 deficient.") %>%
    row_spec(0, 
             bold = TRUE) %>%
    row_spec(3, 
             bold = TRUE) %>%
    column_spec(4, 
                bold = TRUE) %>%
    row_spec(2, hline_after = TRUE) %>%
    kable_styling(font_size = 10)
  
}
if( knitr::is_html_output() ) {
  kable(B12Data,
        format = "html",
        booktabs = TRUE,
        longtable = FALSE,
        align = c("r","r", "r"),
        caption = "The number of vegetarian and non-vegetarian women who are (and are not) B12 deficient.") %>%
    row_spec(0, 
             bold = TRUE) %>%
    row_spec(3, 
             bold = TRUE) %>%
    column_spec(4, 
                bold = TRUE)
}
```




## Data entry {#jamoviChiSquareDataEntry}

In jamovi, the two columns are set up as follows:

* **Diet**: `1` means 'Vegetarian' (i.e. in Row\ 1 of the data table), and `2` means 'Non-vegetarian' (i.e. in Row\ 2 of the data table in Table\ \@ref(tab:jamoviB12Data)).
* **B12**: `1` means 'B12 deficient' (i.e. in Column\ 1 of the data table), and `2` means '*Not* B12 deficient' (i.e. in Column\ 2 of the data table in Table\ \@ref(tab:jamoviB12Data)); see Fig.\ \@ref(fig:jamoviChisqB12DataLong).

The data needs to be set up so that *each row represents one unit of analysis*.
That means there will be $124$ rows of data: one for each person (unit of analysis).

In jamovi, the data are entered as shown in Fig.\ \@ref(fig:jamoviChisqB12DataLong); there are $124$\ rows, but we only show some of these rows to save space.


```{block2, type="rmdimportant"}
Each *row* in the jamovi data represents one *unit of analysis*.

Each *column* in the jamovi data represents one *variable*.
```


```{r jamoviChisqB12DataLong, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="The B12 data entered into jamovi.", fig.align="center", out.width="80%"}
knitr::include_graphics( "jamoviImages/Chisq/B12-Data-Long.png" )
```


```{block2, type="rmdimportant"}
**Note that I entered `1` and `2` into the jamovi worksheet**:
  jamovi just *shows* what these mean in the worksheet, because I have told jamovi what the `1` and the `2` mean.
```


Your data is now set up and ready to use.


## Analysis {#jamoviChiSquareAnalysis}


Remember that **this data set is available from the textbook as `B12-Long`** in [Appendix\ A](https://peterkdunn.github.io/SRM-Textbook/AppendixDataSets.html)


Once the data are entered, we can begin analysis:

1. **Use the menu:** select **Analyses> Frequencies> Independent samples ($\chi^2$ test of association)**

```{r jamoviChisqB12Menu, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Select the correct test.", fig.align="center", out.width="60%"}
knitr::include_graphics( "jamoviImages/Chisq/B12-Menu2.png" )
```



2. **Select the variables:** dragging them from the left panel to the **Rows** and **Columns** areas as appropriate.
In Table\ \@ref(tab:jamoviB12Data), **Diet** is in the rows of the table, for example.


```{r jamoviChisqB12Analysis, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Enter the variables.", fig.align="center", out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics( "jamoviImages/Chisq/B12-Analysis.png" )
```


3. **Select the analysis options:** Under the area where you entered the variables, select the right-pointing arrow beside **Statistics**, and then:

- Select `X2`: this conducts the $\chi^2$ hypothesis test for comparing odds.
- Select `z test for difference in 2 proportions`: this conducts the $z$-test to compare proportions.
- Select `Odds ratio`: this shows the value of the odds ratio.
- Select `Difference in proportions`: this shows the difference between the two proportions.
- Select `Confidence intervals`: this shows the CI for the odds ratio, and for the difference between the proportions.


```{r jamoviChisqB12AnalysisStatsTicks, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Check the correct options.", fig.align="center", out.width="60%"}
knitr::include_graphics( "jamoviImages/Chisq/B12-Analysis-Stats-Ticks.png" )
```

4. You will have your output in the jamovi Output window on the right.





## Numerical summaries {#jamoviChiSquareNumericalSummaries}

*Percentages* can be obtained from the same place: **Analyses> Frequencies Independent samples ($\chi^2$ test of association)**.
Under the area where you selected the **Statistics**, select the right-pointing arrow beside **Cells**, and then:

* Select `Row` under the **Percentages** section; and/or
* Select `Column` under the **Percentages** section.

```{r jamoviChisqB12AnalysisCellsTicks, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Select what to show in the table.", fig.align="center", out.width="60%"}
knitr::include_graphics( "jamoviImages/Chisq/B12-Analysis-Cells-Ticks.png" )
```

Of course, you can select any of the other options too, and see what happens.
